definition: Learning straight-line paths from noise to data and iteratively re-straightening them, so few large steps suffice.
details: Learning straight-line paths from noise to data and iteratively re-straightening them, so few large steps suffice. The flow-matching-family formulation adopted by current flagship image generators for its simplicity and speed (see Flow Matching).

explainer.lead: Rectified flow learns straight-line paths from noise to data and iteratively re-straightens them, so few large steps suffice. It matters for speed and simplicity in generative modeling.

tiers.eli5: Like paving a straight road between two towns so you can drive there in a few long strides instead of many small turns.
tiers.practitioner: Engineers in the flow-matching family train on straight-line couplings and re-straighten, allowing few-step sampling in flagship image generators. A pitfall is assuming few steps always preserve sample quality across every setting.
tiers.paperLevel: Learns straight-line paths from noise to data and iteratively re-straightens them; a flow-matching-family formulation adopted by current flagship image generators for simplicity and speed.

explainer.example: A generator trained with rectified flow produces an image from noise in a handful of large steps rather than many small ones.
